surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Thomas has three assists as the Blues take down the Penguins
paras: Rickard Rakell struck first for the Penguins early in the first. Justin Barron and Dylan Holloway scored a little over four minutes apart in the first half of the second to turn a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 lead. Jimmy Snuggerud made it 3-1 late in the second, and he scored again early in the third to make it 4-1. With the goalie pulled and less than five minutes left, Rakell struck again to cut St. Louis’ lead to 4-2. Holloway scored his second of the night into the empty net with less than three minutes left. The Pens’ Trevor van Riemsdyk was back in the lineup after missing 15 games, and picked up an assist. Robert Thomas finished with three assists.

Don’t let the score fool you: the chances were a lot closer than that. Joel Hofer made 31 saves for the Blues, and Artūrs Šilovs stopped 28 of 32 at the other end. The Blues moved to 11-9-2, seventh in the Central, while the Penguins fell to 7-12-2, sinking to the bottom of the Metropolitan.

items.text: Robert Thomas passed Alex Pietrangelo for third on the Blues’ all-time assists list, with 344.
Robert Thomas has a point in all six of his games against Pittsburgh since 2023-24.
The Penguins have gone winless in five straight at home.
Nick Robertson was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Justin Brazeau played instead.
